items.title: Citrix NetScaler flaw (CVE-2026-88779) under active attack, lands on CISA's KEV list
items.summary: Citrix warned that CVE-2026-88779, a CVSS 8.7 memory-buffer flaw in NetScaler ADC and Gateway appliances configured as SAML service or identity providers, is being actively exploited with no authentication or user interaction required. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on Oct 4, ordering federal agencies to patch by Oct 7; fixed builds are 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28.

items.title: Pentagon confirms personnel data breach affecting more than 3 million people
items.summary: The Pentagon confirmed unauthorized access to a Defense Manpower Data Center information system via a file-sharing vulnerability, exposing records of 2.76 million living people and about 294,000 deceased individuals between Oct 2025 and July 2026. Compromised files contained unencrypted data that could include names, Social Security numbers, and birth dates; affected individuals are being offered a year of credit monitoring.

items.title: PoC released for macOS HFS+ kernel heap overflow (CVE-2026-43682)
items.summary: A public proof-of-concept landed for CVE-2026-43682, a kernel heap overflow in macOS's HFS+ driver where the kernel copies extended-attribute keys from disk without validating their length against the in-memory buffer. Any Mac below macOS Tahoe 26.6, Sequoia 15.7.8, or Sonoma 14.8.8 is exposed; Apple's fix is improved memory handling, and users should avoid mounting disk images from unknown sources until patched.

items.title: Mississippi city shuts down network after ransomware incident; FBI and DHS called in
items.summary: The city of Vicksburg, Mississippi, disconnected its municipal network from the internet on Oct 1 after detecting a ransomware incident, disrupting in-person utility bill payments while 911, police, and fire operations stayed online. The FBI, the Department of Homeland Security, and Mississippi state officials are investigating; whether personal data was compromised is still undetermined.

items.title: Wallstreet ransomware group claims St. Francis Healthcare Systems of Hawaii
items.summary: The Wallstreet ransomware group added St. Francis Healthcare Systems of Hawaii, a Catholic nonprofit serving Hawaii families since 1927, to its leak site on Oct 3. The listing marks another healthcare-sector hit by the group; scope of data theft and the ransom demand have not been disclosed.
